title: IVQ: Structured and Lightweight Vector Quantization via Binary Hierarchical Composition Inspired by $\textit{IChing}$
claim: A small set of binary symbols composes hierarchically into a large structured space, readable consistently from any level of the hierarchy.
layout: Top-down tree with side level labels, plus three bottom view panels
description: A top-down tree diagram rooted at a yin-yang symbol. Each level branches into red solid lines (Yang) and black broken lines (Yin). Level 1 has the two forms, level 2 has four symbols made of two lines, and level 3 has the eight trigrams made of three lines. Each trigram is labeled (Heaven, Lake, Fire and so on). The bottom level shows sixty-four hexagrams made of six lines, with a few examples such as Creative, Receptive, Peace and After/Before Completion, separated by ellipses. A column on the right gives the level names (TaiChi, LiangYi, SiXiang, BaGua, Hexagrams) with downward arrows. Below, the Peace hexagram is expanded into three dotted boxes. They show it as seen from LiangYi, SiXiang and BaGua views, linked by bidirectional arrows. The red and black line pattern draws the eye first.
caption: The core concept of IChing. TaiChi produce LiangYi, LiangYi produce SiXiang, SiXiang produce BaGua, which again produce the sixty-four hexagrams. For each hexagram, it can also interpreted from views of different levels, whether from top to down or from bottom to up.
abstract: Vector Quantization (VQ) has been widely used in visual and audio representation due to its effectiveness in compressing high-dimensional signals. However, existing VQ methods often rely on large and unstructured codebooks, which leads to inefficient code utilization and frequent codebook collapse. In this paper, we propose IChing Vector Quantization (IVQ), a lightweight and structured VQ framework inspired by IChing . IVQ introduces binary hierarchical composition and geometric symmetry relations into the codebook design, enabling a compact set of structured codes to represent the latent space while maintaining high utilization without codebook collapse. Experimental results show that IVQ achieves superior quality with significantly smaller codebooks and consistently higher utilization rates compared to several VQ variants in audio representation. Auxiliary experiments on visual reconstruction and cross-modal generation further validate the universality and robustness of IVQ. Codes are released at https://github.com/chouliuzuo/IVQ.
